text:
yael: quick sanity ping — onbrought a converted Mistral->Gemma variant and seeing a consistent +6% chrF drop on summarization eval vs upstream. latency fine but outputs are hallucinating dates.

yael: suspect rotary/freq handling during our conversion pipeline; model was exported with 'rotary_freq=1.0' but loader applies headwise scaling.

tomas: can you paste the eval snippet and the exact conversion flags?

yael: eval prompt used small summarization set (50 docs), reproducer below:
```
python eval.py --model /mnt/models/gemma-converted/zephyr13b/ --task summarization --quant int4 --batch 1
```
flags during convert: `--from=mistral --to=gemma --preserve-rotary --headwise-scale yes`

nina: did you check tokenization mapping? I've seen off-by-one vocab shifts cause the hallucinations you describe (common when BOS/EOS indices change).

yael: good call — ran quick token-check: first 10 token ids for "2023" differ after conversion (50257 vs 50256).

samir: hm that smells like a vocab-offset + rotary-phase mismatch. If token ids shift, kv-cache indexing + prefix caching can feed wrong rotary angles leading to semantic drift.

yael: attaching tiny log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-21 14:12:01] model_load: rotor_map applied headwise_scale=True
[2026-03-21 14:12:02] vocab_map: offset=+1 applied (preserve_specials=False)
[2026-03-21 14:12:02] eval: chrF=0.623 -> 0.586
```

tomas: can you try two quick experiments: 1) re-run conversion with `--preserve-specials` and 2) force `headwise-scale=False` at load time (our serving runtime accepts `rotary_head_scale: disable`).

yael: running both now, will post numbers.

triage-bot: Reminder: linked issue #INFR-214 added for "rotary/headwise scaling conversion mismatches"

nina: also try diffing rotary base frequency arrays (per-head) from upstream vs converted. small fractional multipliers (0.999 vs 1.0) can amplify on long context.

samir: if the vocab offset is real, simplest mitigation is to remap special token ids first (BOS/EOS/PAD) before applying rotary transforms. We had a patch for this in 2025—should be reusable.

yael: results quick: setting `--preserve-specials` recovered most tokens and chrF jumped back to 0.617. disabling headwise scaling brought chrF to 0.622 (close to upstream). latency identical.

yael: so root cause appears dual: converter applied a +1 offset to non-special tokens and our loader applied headwise scaling by default. combination produced compounding drift.

tomas: nice narrow down. next steps: 1) revert converter default to preserve specials, 2) add a conversion sanity check that validates token ids for common numerals/punctuation, 3) add a loader warning when headwise scaling is enabled for converted models.

samir: I'll open a small PR to the converter with the sanity check and add unit tests for token id invariants.

nina: for rollout: mark the converted artifact as "quarantined" in the model catalog until re-converted, update onboarding checklist to include token id diff step and rotary head frequency compare.

yael: thanks team. I can re-run full eval after PR lands. cc @tomas for follow-on benchmark patch to log rotary arrays during build. :thumbsup:

samir: ack, assigning to samir for PR, nina for catalog update.

triage-bot: Issue #INFR-214 updated: labels added [onboarding, rotary, vocab].

yael: one more note — if you spot similar small chrF deltas on other converted models, please flag immediately; the symptom is usually harmless-looking but impacts hallucination risk.

tomas: will add a lightweight smoke that compares token ids for the ten most frequent tokens and checks rotary frequency norms during conversion.

nina: thanks — saved us from a subtle production regression earlier this year.

yael: closing the loop once PR merged and re-eval done.
